question: Where can I get the current electricity network access tariffs and charges in the United States, by voltage level and period, with their history?

answer.summary: There is no single national table. Transmission access rates are FERC-filed tariffs (eTariff, XML export, versions since 2010) and RTOs post computed rates: PJM zonal NITS in $/MW-year (XLSX), CAISO high/low-voltage access charges in $/MWh (PDF). Distribution charges are in each utility's state-approved tariff, e.g. Oncor (TX) by secondary/primary/transmission service and PG&E (CA) with distribution and transmission components by voltage and TOU period. OpenEI URDB compiles rates nationally but is mostly bundled retail rates.
main_caveats: Transmission (FERC, wholesale) and distribution (state commissions, retail) are regulated separately; no source covers both nationally.
In vertically integrated states retail tariffs are bundled; a network-only charge may not exist as a published value.
Units differ: PJM $/MW-year, CAISO $/MWh, utility tariffs $/kW, $/kWh and $/customer; do not compare without conversion rules.
URDB is a convenience compilation; its voltage tags and start dates can differ from the official tariff.
answer.confidence_reason: Sources tested with downloads, but distribution tariffs and RTO postings were sampled (3 utilities, 2 RTOs); PUCT summary blocked to automated clients.

attributes.note: Transmission: eTariff and RTO postings (PJM, CAISO tested). Distribution: per-utility tariffs, sampled Oncor, PG&E, Con Edison.
attributes.gap_note: No national official compilation found (FERC, PUCT, OpenEI checked). Distribution tariffs tested for 3 utilities only; MISO, SPP, ISO-NE, NYISO postings and other states not opened.

attributes.note: Components separated in sample: PG&E unbundles distribution/transmission; Oncor delivery charges plus TCRF/DCRF riders; CAISO HV/LV TAC.
attributes.gap_note: Separation of network charges was checked only in the sampled tariffs; bundled-rate utilities were not examined individually.

attributes.note: CAISO HV (>=200 kV) vs LV; PG&E and Oncor secondary/primary/transmission service; PJM NITS has no voltage split.
attributes.gap_note: Voltage classes verified in 3 utility tariffs and CAISO only; URDB voltagecategory is empty in 44,320 of 58,920 rows and can contradict the rate name.

attributes.note: PG&E B-19 peak 4-9 p.m., part-peak, off-peak, summer Jun-Sep; Oncor distribution and PJM/CAISO transmission rates have no time bands.
attributes.gap_note: Time-of-use definitions read in PG&E B-19 only; other utilities' calendars not checked (URDB holds 12x24 schedules but unverified).
Latest versions identified only for the tested sources; each other utility or RTO must be checked separately.

attributes.note: eTariff since 2010-10-01; CAISO archive from 2008; PJM files 2021-2026; PG&E B rates from 2019-11-01; URDB rate versions with start dates.
attributes.gap_note: History depth differs by publisher and was only checked for the sampled sources; pre-2010 FERC tariffs (paper era) not checked.

attributes.note: Texas TDU tariffs twice a year (March/September TCRF); URDB annual for ~150 utilities; PJM/CAISO observed several dated postings in 2026.
attributes.gap_note: Stated schedules found only for Texas TDUs (archived PUCT page) and URDB; RTO and other utility schedules only observed, not stated.

sources.name: eTariff Viewer (tariffs filed with FERC, including Open Access Transmission Tariffs)
sources.format: HTML viewer; XML export per tariff (eTariff export schema); RTF/PDF print
sources.summary: FERC's official register of filed tariffs: every FERC-jurisdictional OATT and transmission rate schedule, with section versions and effective dates; XML export per tariff.
sources.coverage_note: Wholesale/interstate transmission service. Not retail distribution tariffs (state PUCs) and not ERCOT-internal utilities.
caveats: Rates are inside tariff text, not typed fields; formula rates need the RTO's posted results.
ferc.gov pages refuse automated clients; etariff.ferc.gov works.

problems: www.ferc.gov and ferc.gov return a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' 403 page to non-browser clients; the etariff.ferc.gov application itself answered normally.
Queries require ASP.NET form posts (view state); there is no documented public API.

example.example_request: curl -s -c cj -b cj https://etariff.ferc.gov/TariffExport.aspx?tid=1763 > page.html; then POST the page's hidden ASP.NET fields plus __EVENTTARGET=ctl00$Content1$btnExport, ctl00$Content1$lstStatus$0=9 (Effective), ctl00$Content1$lstBinaryText$1=2 (plain text) to the same URL with the same cookies

sources.name: RTO/ISO posted transmission service rates (zonal NITS rates, Transmission Access Charge rates)
sources.publisher: Regional transmission organizations / independent system operators (PJM, CAISO tested)
sources.summary: Computed transmission access rates: PJM zonal NITS rates ($/MW-Year, XLSX per period) and CAISO Transmission Access Charge (high-voltage >=200 kV and low-voltage $/MWh, PDF per effective date).
sources.coverage_note: Tested PJM and CAISO; MISO, SPP, ISO-NE, NYISO not opened. Transmission level only.
caveats: CAISO revises sheets for the same effective date; take the latest revision.
PJM NITS rates have no voltage or time-of-day split.

members_summary.scope_note: RTO/ISO markets and transmission providers posting OATT rates; universe not counted in this pass. Tested PJM and CAISO; MISO, SPP, ISO-NE, NYISO and ERCOT were not opened. Utilities outside RTOs post their own OATT rates.
members_summary.pattern: Look on each RTO's billing/settlements or tariff pages for 'transmission service rates', 'zonal rates' or 'revenue requirements'.

sources.name: Utility retail delivery (distribution) tariffs approved by state public utility commissions
sources.publisher: Distribution utilities under state commission approval (Oncor/PUCT, PG&E/CPUC, Con Edison/NYPSC tested)
sources.format: PDF tariff books; some utilities add XLSX rate summaries (PG&E)
sources.summary: Distribution network charges are in each utility's commission-approved tariff: e.g. Oncor (TX) delivery charges by secondary/primary/transmission service; PG&E (CA) B-19 with distribution and transmission components by voltage and TOU period.
sources.coverage_note: Sample of 3 utilities (TX, CA, NY); every other utility publishes its own tariff book.
sources.data_date: Oncor sheets effective 2026-06-01; PG&E B-19 effective 2026-03-01; Con Edison MAC 2026-11-01
caveats: Vertically integrated utilities publish bundled retail rates; network components may not be separated.
Formats and voltage-class definitions differ by utility.

problems: The Texas PUCT site (puc.texas.gov, ftp.puc.texas.gov) returned a Cloudflare block (403) to non-browser requests; the summary of TDU charges was read only through an archived copy of 2024-10-27.

example.example_request: PG&E: https://www.pge.com/tariffs/assets/pdf/tariffbook/ELEC_SCHEDS_B-19.pdf, sheet Cal. P.U.C. 61072-E (UNBUNDLING OF TOTAL RATES), pdftotext -layout
example.example_result: Distribution**: Maximum Demand Summer $28.24 (R) $19.98 (R) $7.81 (R) [Secondary, Primary, Transmission voltage, $ per kW]; Transmission Maximum Demand* $9.10 $9.10 $9.10; Advice 7846-E, Effective March 1, 2026

members_summary.scope_note: One tariff book per regulated distribution utility (investor-owned utilities regulated by each state commission; many cooperatives and municipal utilities set their own rates). Tested one large utility in each of Texas, California and New York; other states and utilities not checked.
members_summary.pattern: Search the utility site for 'tariff', 'rate schedules' or 'Tariff for Retail Delivery Service'; check the state commission's tariff filings for official leaves.

sources.name: U.S. Utility Rate Database (URDB)
sources.publisher: OpenEI / National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR, U.S. Department of Energy laboratory)
sources.format: CSV (gzip) and JSON (gzip); REST API with key
sources.license: Creative Commons Zero (CC0) unless otherwise noted
sources.summary: National CC0 compilation of utility rate structures (energy, demand, fixed, TOU calendars, voltage category, start/end dates); bulk CSV of 58,920 rate versions downloaded 2026-11-26.
sources.coverage_note: Mostly total retail rates; only 3,252 rows marked Delivery; voltagecategory empty in 75% of rows.
caveats: Not an official register; verify against the source tariff.
Voltage tags and start dates can differ from the tariff.

example.example_request: curl -sLO https://openei.org/apps/USURDB/download/usurdb.csv.gz ; python: csv.DictReader over gzip, filter eiaid=='14328' and 'B-19' in name, sort by startdate

if_unstructured.summary: Outside the PJM and PG&E spreadsheets, rate values are inside PDF tariff sheets; extract the schedule table per utility.

local_terms.meaning: FERC-filed tariff with transmission service terms and rates; searchable in eTariff.
Texas TDU tariff containing distribution delivery charges by service voltage.
PG&E tariff section splitting each charge into generation, distribution and transmission components.
PJM zonal transmission rate in $/MW-year posted by PJM settlements.
CAISO high-voltage and low-voltage transmission charge in $/MWh.
Texas transmission and distribution cost recovery factor riders adjusting delivery charges.
Transmission and distribution utility / service provider in Texas retail choice areas.
Service voltage classes used in US retail tariffs; definitions vary by utility.

provenance.note: Minutes are researcher estimates. Counts describe documented passes, not publication approval. Missing history or effort is not reconstructed.
